rationale: The claim that wave-packet spatial evolution in a gravitational field depends on the ratio of gravitational to inertial mass is a quantum-mechanical specialization of the universality of free fall encompassed by the equivalence principle. The meta-principle supplies the physical basis for treating gravitational and inertial mass as equivalent, while the new principle applies that relation to quantum wave-packet dynamics.

rationale: The NP-hardness claim for connected bipartite graphs of maximum degree three is obtained by a polynomial-time reduction from a known NP-hard problem. The reduction-completeness meta-principle is the general statement that such reductions transfer worst-case hardness to the target problem, so it directly supports the theorem.
